run.task: Item #9: live-verify the remaining trash flows (journal post enum cast, promo code, shipping zone) and confirm route presence for all 13 controllers.

criteria.statement: Given the 13 trash controllers, when inspected, then each exposes /deleted, /{id}/restore and /{id}/permanent.
criteria.notes: 13/13 controllers expose all three endpoints; JournalController also exposes the journal-categories variants.

criteria.statement: Given a trashed journal post with status PUBLISHED, when the trash listing is called, then the row appears with status = PUBLISHED (enum cast succeeded).
criteria.notes: Seeded a DRAFT/PUBLISHED post via SQL, called the endpoint, status came back as 'PUBLISHED'. The JournalPostStatus.valueOf((String) row[4]) cast only fails on a real JDBC row, so this live check is the only way to prove it.

criteria.statement: Given a trashed promo code, when the trash listing is called, then it appears and disappears correctly after restore.
criteria.notes: SAVE20 soft-deleted -> appeared in trash -> restored -> gone. Exercises the entity-pattern (not folded rows) trash listing.

criteria.statement: Given a trashed shipping zone, when the trash listing is called, then it appears and disappears correctly after restore.
criteria.notes: Cairo Zone soft-deleted -> appeared in trash -> restored -> gone.

criteria.statement: Given the 8 remaining trash entities (BrewingMethod, CoffeeVariety, Farm, Origin, Pairing, ProcessingMethod, RoastLevel, TastingNote), when inspected, then they follow the same safe pattern (SoftDeleteRowFolder.fold, only Number/String/Instant/Boolean casts, no enum valueOf).
criteria.notes: 8/8 follow the identical pattern; no enum casts, only Number/String/Instant/Boolean. The Journal enum cast (N-02) was separately proven live.
